notes:
39 station rows (lines 5903–5950). There are no sub-headings inside the list, so I set coast to the section title, "IRISH COAST", for every row.

How the columns were read: the four columns after the name are Spring mark, Autumn mark, miles from shore and observers. I put the first three in `other` as "Sp. …; Au. …; miles from shore …". "--" in the Sp./Au. columns seems to mean no schedule was sent that season. "--" in the miles column probably means a shore station. "½" (Dursey Island) is printed as a fraction.

Checks against the abbreviations:
- 35 rows have at least one season with a schedule sent. Without Lough Swilly (Sp. --) that leaves 34 for spring, and without Oyster Island (Au. --) 34 for autumn. Both match "34 schedules sent out".
- I count 27 x in Sp. and 25 x in Au., which matches the stated replies.

Things a reader should know:
- Numbering: 5 and 8 each appear twice. The second of each, Coningbeg and Arklow North (both Lt.-ship), has "*" before its name. The list gives no key for the asterisk. There is no 9, 35 or 36.
- "do." (ditto) is the printed place for Barrels Rock, Tuskar Rock and Arklow North. I kept it as printed. It stands for Wexford, Wexford and Wicklow.
- "Old Head, Kinsale, Cork": I took "Old Head, Kinsale" as the name and "Cork" as the place. Only Fastnet has "Co. Cork"; the other Cork rows just say "Cork".
- "Oyster Island, N. Sligo" has no comma after N., unlike "Eagle Island, E., Mayo". So I read "N. Sligo" as the place and "Oyster Island" as the name.
- I dropped the comma that separates the name from the place, so "Eagle Island, E., Mayo," gives name "Eagle Island, E." and place "Mayo".
- Braces "{": these only group observer names that wrap onto a second line. They don't mark the station, so I left `marks` null for those rows. They are kept in the fragments.
- "_No reply._" (Old Head, Howth Baily, Oyster Island) and "No schedule sent." (Eagle Island W., Slyne Head S., Arran Island S., Dursey Island) appear in the observer column. I put them in `other` and left keepers empty. "No schedule sent." is not in italics.
- Blackrock's observer "J. Young" is split across two lines ("J." / "Young,"). I gave it as one keeper.
- "Edward M'Carron" is named at both Mine Head (4) and Tearaght (37). This could be one keeper who moved during the year, or two different men.
- "Lough Swilly" names no particular light. It is probably Fanad Head or Buncrana; the list only gives "Lough Swilly".
- Spellings kept as printed: Innishtrahull (Inishtrahull), Howth Baily (Baily), Arran Island N./S. (Aran / Inisheer), Arranmore, Robert Tyrell, Thomas Kerley, John Pinston, "Arklow Sth." The list gives no characters for any light.
